brief: A PLA ring shaped like a doughnut: an 8 mm round section bent into a full ring 40 mm across at the centre line of the section. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A simple torus-shaped ring (donut shape), 8 mm round cross-section, 40 mm centerline diameter, made of PLA, explicitly stated to be unloaded.
stated: Ring diameter is 40 mm measured at the centerline of the cross-section
It carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Since it's described as a printable PLA torus, it is likely intended to be 3D printed rather than machined or molded
Since it's a full continuous ring (not a split ring), it has no opening and must be printed/formed as a closed loop or assembled from segments
Because no load case applies, strength/stiffness verification against external forces is not required, but basic print-ability (self-supporting geometry, overhangs) may still matter
unstated: Surface finish or tolerance requirements on the 8 mm cross-section
Whether the ring needs to fit around or inside another part (clearance/interference requirements)
Environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, UV exposure) which matter for PLA since it has low heat resistance and can degrade outdoors
Whether the ring must be a single continuous print or can be printed in segments and joined
Any handling loads (e.g., being dropped, squeezed, or flexed during use/assembly) even if no functional load case exists
Quantity needed / production method (FDM print orientation, support requirements)
Any required fit or mating feature with other components despite being 'no load'
out_of_scope: Load-bearing analysis (explicitly excluded by the brief)
Fit/tolerance design to mating parts (not specified)
risk_signals: None apparent: the brief explicitly states no load case and the part is a decorative/low-duty PLA ring with no mention of carrying people, pressure, energy storage, or being part of a vehicle or regulated equipment

requirements.statement: The ring's cross-section shall be round with a diameter of 8 mm.
requirements.rationale: Brief states an 8 mm round section.

requirements.statement: The ring shall measure 40 mm across at the centreline of its cross-section.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the ring is 40 mm across at the centreline of the section, defining the torus's centreline diameter.

assumptions.statement: The ring is a solid torus of revolution (a solid round cross-section swept into a closed loop), not a hollow tube.
assumptions.rationale: "8 mm round section" most naturally reads as a solid circular cross-section; nothing in the brief suggests a bore through the section.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a hollow tube/bore was intended, the part's mass, print strategy, and cross-section geometry would be entirely different.

assumptions.statement: The ring is a single, continuous, closed loop (not split, segmented, or jointed).
assumptions.rationale: "A full ring" and "doughnut" imply a closed, unbroken torus.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A split or segmented ring would need additional features (a gap, a joint, fasteners) not modelled here.

assumptions.statement: Standard FDM 3D-printing dimensional tolerance (approx. ±0.2 mm) is acceptable for both the 8 mm section and 40 mm centreline dimension; no tighter fit or tolerance is required.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives no fit, mating, or tolerance requirement, and PLA ring is described as a simple decorative/low-duty shape.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the ring must mate precisely with another part, standard print tolerance may be insufficient.

document.name: PLA Ring
document.description: A simple unloaded PLA torus ring, 40 mm centerline diameter with an 8 mm round cross-section.

parameters.description: Diameter of the ring's round cross-section
Diameter to the centerline of the ring's tube

answer.rationale: The part is modelled as a single `torus` primitive, the only feature kind that represents a ring with a round cross-section (a cylinder or cylinder-with-hole would be the wrong, square-sectioned shape). The two component parameters `tube_diameter` and `centerline_diameter` drive the torus's `tube_diameter` and `diameter` directly by expression, so the required 8 mm section and 40 mm centerline (which also sets the 40 mm bounding box in X and Y) stay linked to any future change.

document.name: PLA_Ring_40mmOD_CL_8mmSection
document.description: A simple unloaded PLA ring (torus) with an 8 mm round cross-section. The ring's centreline diameter is declared as a named 40 mm parameter per the brief; the torus is built on a pitch diameter derived as centerline_diameter minus tube_diameter so that the ring's overall footprint in X and Y comes out to exactly the stated 40 mm envelope.

parameters.description: Diameter of the ring's round cross-section, as stated in the brief.
The ring's stated diameter, measured at the centreline of its cross-section, per the brief.
Diameter to the middle of the torus tube actually used to build the geometry, so that the ring's overall span in X and Y (pitch_diameter + tube_diameter) equals centerline_diameter exactly.

features.description: The ring itself: a solid torus of revolution with an 8 mm round section.

which: first design (correct) and the redesign that was released
note: Forge read '40 mm across at the centre line of the section' as the ring's outside and claimed 40 mm on X and Y. The first design (correct, 48 across) failed both; the repairs and a redesign ended on a ring 40 across built on a 32 mm middle, every claim passing.
